conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced turned up. Elastic's habit of beating its own guide (Q1 revenue $478M against a $469-470M guide) is already in a consensus sitting at the top of the Q2 guide, with the whisper above it. Two observability peers that beat this season (DDOG, DT) were sold 14-16% on their guides, and TD Cowen's cautious channel checks lean the reaction slightly negative. A 20% slide in 20 days has lowered the bar, so the net is a coin flip at p_up 48 on a ~17% move. The findings sum (-0.9) and the scaled number (-0.68) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q2 FY27 total revenue $486.7-486.8M and non-GAAP EPS $0.81 (MarketBeat $486.77M / $0.809, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-elastic-estc-projected-to-post-earnings-on-thursday-2026-11-12/ ; Earnings Whispers via Finviz $486.7M / $0.81, whisper $0.88, https://finviz.com/news/421334/elastic-must-show-its-revenue-reacceleration-has-legs-after-a-16-post-earnings-slide). This sits at the top of the company's guide: revenue $486-487M, sales-led subscription $407.5-408.5M, non-GAAP operating margin ~19%, EPS $0.80-0.82; FY27 revenue $1.998-2.010B, EPS $3.29-3.37 (https://www.01net.it/elastic-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results/). Two estimate sources agree with each other and with the guide, so the bar is sourced. The sweep row's '$0.14 consensus' and Benzinga's '$0.68' are stale or GAAP and are disowned. The real bar is a FY guide raise: TD Cowen expects a modest sales-led beat plus a matching raise.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 4.74M shares with 2.6 days to cover as of the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/estc), roughly 4.5% of the 105.98M shares outstanding at the 2026-09-17 record date (8-K 2026-10-15). That is not a crowded short. No settlement after September was found. The baseline's 25-delta skew is null (no directional statement from options). Put/call open interest is 0.15, so call-heavy. The straddle implies a 17.05% move against a 14.67% median of the last 7 prints. Tape: -11.42% over 5 days, -19.67% over 20, -26% from the 52-week high. Earnings Whispers (Nov 11) put bearish sentiment at 28.6%, down from 46.3% before the last print.

findings.finding: Elastic beats its own guide by about 1.5-2% of revenue and beats its margin guide. In Q1 FY27 revenue was $478M against a $469-470M guide (+1.7%) and sales-led subscription $399M against $392-393M; the operating margin of 16.2% and EPS of $0.70 compared with roughly $0.58 consensus, and FY revenue was raised by about $12M at the midpoint. The Q2 consensus ($486.7M, EPS $0.81) sits at the top of a $486-487M / $0.80-0.82 guide. Repeating Q1's beat implies about $494M (+1.5% against the bar) and EPS in the high $0.80s.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise prints have gone both ways. Aug 2026 (Q1 beat, FY raise): +19.3%. May 2026: +12.3%. Nov 2025 (beat and raise, 'cautious FY26 outlook'): -14.7%. Feb 2026: -15.4%. The reported-quarter beat alone has not decided the sign; the guide and the sector tape have.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. If the market expected only the guide, consensus would sit at the $486.5M midpoint and not the top; the $0.88 whisper above the $0.82 guide top shows a beat is expected. The residual is only how large the beat is.
findings.independence: Q1 guide figures come from a different document, the Q4 FY26 release (https://businesswire.com/news/home/20260527847546/en/Elastic-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Financial-Results). The management line 'we've always taken a prudent and risk-adjusted view to guidance' is in the Q1 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15497663695938560). All three are company documents describing one habit.

findings.finding: Leading indicators support a further FY27 guide raise. In Q1, cRPO grew 21% (20% cc) to $1.153B and RPO 27% to $1.854B, both ahead of 15% revenue growth. Management said growth accelerates through FY27 with Q4 the highest, and that the FY guide is back-half weighted. 37% of $100K+ customers use AI features (21% a year earlier), and $100K+ customers rose to over 1,800 on record net adds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026: the FY raise with cRPO +21% bought +19.3%. Nov 2025: a raise judged cautious sold -14.7%. Peer raises this season (DDOG, DT) were sold, so the size of the raise relative to the whisper decides it.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell side expects a raise: TD Cowen expects a 'matching raise', and the Earnings Whispers preview names another raise as needed. The 20% slide since Nov 1 says the market doubts the raise will be big enough, or pays less for it. Unpriced would look like a stock trading as if growth stalled at 15%. It is partly priced, so the finding is small.
findings.independence: The same release reports the cRPO and RPO figures (https://www.01net.it/elastic-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results/), so this is one company source; it shares the Q1 documents with the first finding, on a different line.

findings.finding: This season's observability peers beat and were sold on their guides. Datadog (Nov 4) beat on revenue ($1.20B, +35%, against $1.14B) and EPS, guided Q4 flat with Q3, and fell 14-16%. Dynatrace (Nov 3) beat on revenue and margin, but net new ARR was flat year on year and it cut FY EPS guidance to $1.88-1.90 from $1.97-1.99; the stock fell more than 14% premarket. The market is punishing beats in this group that lack an above-whisper forward guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ESTC's own Nov 2025 print (beat and raise, -14.7%) followed the same pattern: the beat was sold on the outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: ESTC's 20% slide since the peers printed partly prices a de-rating, but the reaction function for this print (beats sold) is not something a lower price removes. If the market expected a sell-the-beat, the straddle would not be priced above ESTC's own 14.7% median; at 17%, it is pricing a big move with no skew.
findings.independence: Dynatrace: https://finimize.com/content/dynatrace-beat-q2-forecasts-then-spooked-investors-with-guidance and https://finviz.com/news/414433/dynatrace-beats-on-revenue-and-margin-but-stalled-net-new-arr-and-arize-dilution-cloud-the-outlook (Nov 2026). These are two different companies' prints, but they show the market's reaction function, not ESTC's numbers.

findings.finding: TD Cowen (Nov 17) cut its price target to $85 from $95 and kept Hold. It cited 'cautious industry checks', particular caution on Observability, declining third-party sales-rep reviews, insider sales above $400M, and expectations that 'have risen slightly' since last quarter. It still expects a modest beat on sales-led subscription growth (against the 17% guide) and a matching FY raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured history of ESTC reacting to a channel-check note. The stock fell 6.3% on Nov 17, the same day the IGV fell 3.4%, so the note's own effect cannot be separated from the sector move.
findings.why_not_priced: The note is on the wire two days before the print, so it is partly priced. What it adds is a channel check on observability pipeline and sales-rep sentiment, which no consensus number carries. If its checks were fully priced, the consensus would sit below the guide top; it does not.
findings.independence: Defense World repeats the same note (https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/11/18/elastic-nyseestc-given-new-85-00-price-target-at-td-cowen.html), which is the same source. Partly independent: Cisco's observability growth of +2% (Nov 12) also shows a soft observability market. Contrary: Citi raised its target to $132 from $128 with a Buy (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/11/15/elastic-nyseestc-price-target-raised-to-132-00.html).

findings.finding: Hyperscaler infrastructure accelerated in the Sep-quarter (Q3 2026): AWS grew 39.3%, its fastest in almost five years and its sixth straight quarter of acceleration; Azure grew 48%. Elastic Cloud runs on all three hyperscalers and is sold through their marketplaces, and annual Elastic Cloud revenue grew 27% in Q1 (26% the quarter before). That is a consumption tailwind for the cloud part of sales-led revenue in the Aug-Oct quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no ESTC-specific history on hyperscaler read-through. Datadog posted 35% growth on the same backdrop and was still sold on its guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Q3 2026 results, per URL path and text)
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro proxy that every software investor has seen, so it is mostly priced. It is unconfirmed by Elastic for this quarter: management called cloud 'not a guided metric' that 'varies quarter to quarter'.
findings.independence: Synergy Research puts cloud infrastructure services growth at 55% for the quarter (https://www.telecomtv.com/content/digital-platforms-services/ai-drives-cloud-services-sector-growth-to-55-in-q3-56566/). It is a proxy and not a company number.

findings.finding: Cisco's Q1 FY27 (Nov 12, quarter ended Oct 24, roughly overlapping Elastic's Aug-Oct quarter) put observability growth at +2% and security at +7% (Splunk is inside both), well below Cisco's own high-single-digit FY27 projection. Splunk is Elastic's main competitor in logs and SIEM. Weak Splunk is consistent with Elastic taking share in SIEM and logs, but also with soft observability budgets.
findings.why_not_priced: Few readers translate Cisco's segment line to Elastic, but the sign is ambiguous, so its size is near zero.
findings.independence: The +2% observability and +7% security figures come from Futurum's breakdown (https://futurumgroup.com/?p=97973). Cuts the other way: TD Cowen's cautious observability checks.

findings.finding: The stock has de-rated about 20% in 20 sessions, mostly with the sector, which lowers the bar going in. It went from $87.25 (Nov 10) to $80.39 (Nov 17, -6.3% on a day the IGV fell 3.4%, its fifth 3%+ drop since Oct 16) to $78.89 at the seal. The drivers were AI-agent disruption fears, the Anthropic IPO (pricing Nov 18, trading Nov 19) and GPT-6.2 releases. Earnings Whispers bearish sentiment had eased to 28.6% from 46.3% before the slide. Put/call OI is 0.15 and short interest about 4.5% of shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: ESTC fell 15.4% on a sector-wide day (Block layoffs, Anthropic Managed Agents). Sector tape has dominated this name's reactions in risk-off weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is in the price by definition; the question is whether a clean raise reverses it. A crowded short would show up as SI above 10%, and it is not there. The Anthropic IPO's first trading days fall inside the window and can keep sector pressure on, which is why the range is wide in both directions.
findings.independence: The price path ($87.25 Nov 10, $80.39 Nov 17) is from GuruFocus (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9206309/a-look-at-elastic-nv-estc-after-63-decline-gf-value-11113-vs-price-8039), and the sentiment reading from Earnings Whispers (https://finviz.com/news/421334/elastic-must-show-its-revenue-reacceleration-has-legs-after-a-16-post-earnings-slide).

findings.finding: MarketBeat counts insider selling last quarter at 4,585,641 shares worth $422.9M, about 4.3% of shares outstanding. Form 4s include CTO/founder Shay Banon selling about 84,200 shares at roughly $84.50-85.30 on Sep 14 and the CRO selling 10,000 at $92.58 on Oct 2. The CEO's Sep 9 sale was sell-to-cover. findings.why_not_priced: It is public and aggregated, so it is mostly priced. The residual is a supply overhang on any post-print rally.
findings.independence: The Form 4s are on SEC (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001707753/000112329226001296/form4.xml), and TD Cowen's note cites more than $400M. The note and the aggregator draw on the same filings.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. The small negative lean agrees with the 20-day slide and the peers' sell-the-beat reactions, so it is probably partly priced. The positive company-level facts (guide beats, cRPO above revenue growth) are also what consensus and the whisper already carry, so the net sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 / 'two readings of one document': merged the draft's revenue-beat (+0.5) and margin/EPS-beat (+0.3) findings, which both rest on Q1's conservative-guidance habit in one release, into one finding at +0.4. The bar sits at the guide top, so the beat lands inside what the company told the market to expect.

Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): cut the cRPO/guide-raise finding from +0.5 to +0.4, given ESTC's split history on beat-and-raise prints and the peers' sold raises. The peer sell-the-beat finding stays at -1.5.
Lesson 5 (proxy small, filed): hyperscaler finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4. The Cisco/Splunk proxy stays +0.2 as an ambiguous proxy.
Lesson 7: short interest checked before the negatives (about 4.5%, 2.6 days, not crowded), so no shrink for squeeze risk.
Lesson 8 / core 3b (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 16 to 17, the option-implied move. p_up moved from 49 to 48 because the merge removed a positive.
